column1: # What counts as a credential, once, for everything orgami screens or redacts:
# the note screen (orgami note, notes --check, screen, sync) refuses text that
# matches any row, and the session digest sent to a model has every match
# replaced by [redacted] first. lib/secrets.sh reads this file.
# One row per shape: name <TAB> flags <TAB> pattern. The name is what a refused
# note is told it matched. Flags are jq's regex flags: `i` for case-insensitive,
# `-` for none. The pattern is a jq (Oniguruma) regex, not grep -E: \b,
# lookahead and inline (?-i:...) mean the same on every platform there, and
# they do not under GNU and BSD grep and sed.
# A named group `keep` survives redaction, so `TOKEN=` stays readable and only
# the value goes. Values that are plainly placeholders — $VAR, ${VAR}, <value>,
# %s, *** — are not credentials and do not match, so a note can still say
# A name that ends in _path, _url, _id, _ttl, tokens and the like holds where a
# secret lives or how big it is, not the secret, and does not match.
# It is spelt [f][i]le there because under `i` jq 1.6 folds "fi" into the one-
# character ligature, and refuses a look-behind whose length is then unsure.
# A row added here needs a positive and a negative case in test/secrets_test.sh.
